summary: SolaceThera production streams: intermittent silent segments and load-balancer resets causing elevated latency and billing spike
summary_long: During a high-throughput nightly batch window for SolaceThera, customers observed repeated silent gaps in streaming completions (client receives initial tokens then a prolonged silence, followed by a full non-streaming completion). This coincided with a spike in downstream token billing because many requests fell back to synchronous completions and some clients retried. Issue traced to intermittent TCP RSTs emitted by a leased load-balancer due to ephemeral connection table exhaustion on the customer-dedicated edge pool.
description:
Issue summary:
SolaceThera reported multiple user sessions on prod-us-east where streaming responses paused for 6-20s mid-completion, after which the SDK received a full non-streaming response. Impact included degraded UX for real-time features, replayed client retries, and an unexpected billing surge for the last 6 hours of the customer's billing window.

Impact:
- ~18% of streaming requests from SolaceThera returned a silent segment during the 23:00-05:00 UTC window on 2026-03-08.
- Customers saw increased average P95 latency for chat endpoints from 120ms to ~1.8s.
- Billing anomaly: SolaceThera's hourly token usage increased by ~32% in the affected window.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted (customer pinned to dedicated edge pool)
- Region: us-east
- Model: redwood-ggml-14b-q4_0 quantized variant

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Client opens streaming completion (HTTP/2 + chunked frames).
2) Initial token stream begins normally.
3) After ~10-50 tokens, stream pauses (no DATA frames).
4) After 6-20s either the connection resets or client stops reading; SDK reattempts non-streaming call.
5) Non-streaming completion returns full response; duplicate token accounting occurs due to overlap.

Observed behavior vs expected:
- Observed: mid-stream silence, then fallback synchronous completion or duplicate completion when clients retry.
- Expected: continuous streaming until completion or graceful streaming termination with explicit error code.

Relevant logs/metrics:
- Edge LB metrics show short TCP RST bursts originating from a subset of dedicated edge hosts (d-edge-us-east-12..16) around 2026-03-08T23:20Z–2026-03-09T04:15Z.
- Serving runtime trace correlation id: sol-epoch-20260308-23-{traceId} (see linked Slack thread for full trace list).
- Token accounting traces indicate an overlap window where streaming tokens and subsequent non-streaming tokens were both billed in ~1.2% of affected requests.

Customer impact and escalation:
- SolaceThera SRE (Escalation lead: Priya Kapoor) opened a high-priority support call at 2026-03-09 00:10 UTC.
- Business impact: real-time triage workflows delayed for clinicians during the 4-hour window. Customer requested immediate mitigation, billing credit, and a post-incident action plan.
comments: 2026-03-08 23:45 - Maya Chen (Support): Acknowledged issue and opened incident bridge. Notified #support and #incidents. Requested SolaceThera SDK logs and sample request IDs.

2026-03-09 00:05 - Arjun Patel (SRE): Initial triage indicates spike in TCP RSTs from dedicated edge hosts. Rotating pool members off those hosts as temporary mitigation. Hypothesis: connection table exhaustion on edge LB caused by batch prefetch pattern from customer's integration.

2026-03-09 00:22 - Priya Kapoor (SolaceThera SRE): Provided SDK traces showing stream pause at token 34 for request id sol-req-16342. Confirmed retries were client-side after SDK watchdog timeout. Asked for immediate rollback of last load-balancer config change (none in control plane since 2026-03-07).

2026-03-09 01:10 - Arjun Patel (SRE): Scoped the issue to specific dedicated edge hosts and applied transient throttling at L4 for new connections from SolaceThera's IP range to smooth the burst. Observed reduction in RSTs after throttle. Adding connection tracking tuning as next step.

2026-03-09 03:40 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer accepted temporary throttle mitigation; requested formal credit estimate for billing surge. Opened linked billing ticket SUP-200742 for credit estimate.

2026-03-10 10:00 - Arjun Patel (SRE): Deployed permanent fix: increased conntrack table sizes on dedicated edge pool, added backpressure window to streaming-proxy to limit per-client concurrent prefetched streams, and pushed a control-plane rule to gracefully reject when pool saturation approaches 85%.

2026-03-11 09:30 - Maya Chen (Support): Post-incident sync call with SolaceThera. Shared technical root cause and mitigation timeline. Customer requested two action items: (1) SDK watchdog default increase and (2) billing credit of one affected billing hour. Ticket marked resolved pending credit confirmation.
investigation_notes: Edge telemetry: RST bursts align with kernel-level conntrack overflow counters on dedicated hosts. No serving-runtime OOMs or model kernel errors observed.

Traffic analysis: SolaceThera's integration executes scheduled parallel prefetch of 40 concurrent streaming sessions per instance at 23:00 UTC; average customer burst ~3x higher than typical production tenants causing ephemeral connection table pressure.
SDK behavior: client SDK treats prolonged lack of stream frames as stall and issues a synchronous retry; race window leads to double token accounting in small subset of flows.
Hypothesis validated by repro: simulated 40x concurrent streaming sessions against a single edge host reproduces mid-stream silence and conntrack overflow within 90s.
root_cause: Dedicated edge load-balancer connection table exhaustion under a high parallel prefetch pattern from SolaceThera, leading to transient TCP RSTs and client-side retries that produced silent streaming segments and duplicate token accounting.
resolution_summary: Applied immediate transient throttling for SolaceThera's IP range to reduce burst; increased conntrack table sizes and added per-client prefetch limits on streaming-proxy; introduced control-plane saturation threshold (85%) to proactively reject new streaming sessions. Coordinated an SDK-config suggestion for the customer to increase the watchdog timeout to reduce synchronous fallbacks. Billing ticket created for crediting the affected hour.
resolution_steps: 2026-03-09 00:40 - Applied transient L4 throttling for customer burst — reduced RSTs by ~90%.
2026-03-09 18:20 - Tuned conntrack parameters on dedicated edge hosts (d-edge-us-east-12..16) and rolled restart in controlled fashion.
2026-03-10 10:00 - Deployed streaming-proxy change to enforce per-client concurrent prefetch cap of 12 streams and added backpressure signalling to SDKs.
2026-03-10 10:05 - Control-plane rule: reject new streaming session when pool saturation >= 85% with explicit 429 body to encourage client backoff.
2026-03-11 09:00 - Customer SDK recommended change: increase streaming watchdog from 5s to 15s for their integration; customer agreed to stagger prefetch schedule.
postincident_actions: Create a synthetic canary that simulates large parallel prefetch patterns against each dedicated edge pool (owner: SRE). Due by 2026-04-01.
Add conntrack saturation alert with automated mitigation runbook (owner: Network SWAT). Due by 2026-03-20.
Formalize customer-facing guidance for prefetch/backoff patterns in the Dedicated onboarding doc (owner: Developer Experience). Due by 2026-04-05.
Billing action: credit one full affected billing hour for SolaceThera and confirm closure on SUP-200742 (owner: Finance Ops). Due by 2026-03-14.
SDK change: introduce explicit server-sent stall code and update SDK default watchdog to 15s to avoid unnecessary synchronous retries (owner: SDK). RFC opened: PR#12345.
resolution_notes_additional: Customer accepted technical rationale and temporary credit offer. Follow-up items scheduled and tracked via linked tasks. Case closed after confirming no recurrence for 48h and billing credit applied.
customer_communication: 2026-03-11 Email to SolaceThera (Maya Chen): detailed post-incident report attached, technical root cause, permanent mitigations applied, requested confirmation of acceptance for billing credit. Customer replied: 'Thank you — mitigation accepted; will stagger prefetch and update SDK. Appreciate the credit.'
